items.content:
Signal Flow

All sensors communicate via I2C at 400kHz. The ESP32-S3 acts as bus master.

- SHT40: polled every 2s
- LIS3DH: interrupt-driven (GPIO6)
- EEPROM: config storage on boot

BLE advertising every 1s in active mode.

items.content:
Regulator Selection

Primary: TPS63020 (TI)
- Buck-boost, 96% efficiency
- 3.3V output, 2A max
- Input: 1.8V-5.5V

Alternatives evaluated:
- TPS63802: newer, smaller (2x1.5mm) but $$
- AP3429: cheaper, buck-only (no LiPo deep discharge)

Decision: Keep TPS63020 unless lead-time forces change.

items.content:
Battery Life Estimate

Active (BLE TX):  350mA x 5ms  = 1.75mAs/event
Idle (sensors):    12mA x 100ms = 1.2mAs/cycle
Deep sleep:        12uA

At 1 event/sec:
  Avg = ~15mA
  500mAh / 15mA = 33 hours

At 0.1 event/sec (low power):
  Avg = ~2mA
  500mAh / 2mA = 250 hours (~10 days)

items.content:
Thermal Management Notes

The ESP32-S3 dissipates approximately 1.2W during sustained BLE+WiFi TX at maximum power. The WROOM-1 module's metal shield acts as a modest heatsink, but in an enclosed plastic housing we expect junction temps to rise significantly.

Measured Thermals (Rev 2.0 prototype):
Ambient 25C, no airflow, ABS enclosure:
- ESP32 shield: 52C (steady state, BLE only)
- ESP32 shield: 68C (WiFi+BLE concurrent)
- TPS63020: 41C (350mA continuous load)
- SHT40: 28C (self-heating <0.1C at 1 meas/sec)

Recommendations for Rev 2.1:
1. Add 4x thermal vias (0.3mm) under ESP32 GND pad, connected to internal GND plane
2. Increase copper pour on top layer around power section — target 30% fill
3. Consider 0.5mm FR4 core to reduce thermal resistance to bottom layer
4. SHT40 placement: maintain 3mm clearance from any heat source. Current placement (bottom-left) is acceptable.
5. Add thermal relief pattern on battery connector pads to prevent cold joints during reflow.

The thermal simulation (ANSYS Icepak) shows peak junction temp of 85C under worst-case conditions (WiFi+BLE, 45C ambient, sealed enclosure). This is within the -40 to +105C operating range but leaves limited margin. Recommend functional testing at 60C ambient to validate.

Reference: Espressif Technical Note TN-0001 'Thermal Design Guidelines for ESP32 Modules'

- OTA update mechanism via BLE
- Watchdog timer, brownout detection
- Production test mode (all LEDs, all sensors, RSSI)

Notes:
- Use ESP-IDF v5.2 (not Arduino framework)
- Alex owns FW, Sarah reviews PRs
- CI pipeline: build + static analysis on every push

items.content:
BLE GATT Service Definition

Service UUID: 0x181A (Environmental Sensing)

Characteristics:
- Temperature (0x2A6E): sint16, units 0.01 C
- Humidity (0x2A6F): uint16, units 0.01 %RH  
- Accel X/Y/Z (custom): sint16[3], units mg
- Battery Level (0x2A19): uint8, 0-100%
- Device Name (0x2A00): utf8s, max 20 chars

Advertising:
- Interval: 1000ms (normal), 200ms (fast connect)
- Payload: flags + complete local name + service UUID
- TX Power: 0dBm (default), +9dBm (long range)

Security:
- Bonding: yes (store up to 4 peers)
- MITM: no (no display/keyboard)
- Encryption: AES-128-CCM

See: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bluetooth_Low_Energy#Software_model
